report: 26-year-old male with a 6-year painless neck lump that recently grew rapidly, firm grade III goiter, and cervical lymphadenopathy. Normal calcitonin and thyroid antibodies refute medullary and autoimmune thyroiditis. Pathologist and laboratory analyses favor malignant thyroid tumor (0.65) over benign nodular goiter (0.60). Papillary carcinoma is leading subtype (0.45), fitting young age and lymphadenopathy. FNA, IHC, surgical pathology are pending; papillary carcinoma remains the leading diagnosis.
